labour.10.1: SUL STC NAS LIF HF EUR
labour.10.why: Divides camps that treat strikes as a disruptive breach of social peace (to be minimised) from those that see them as a legitimate lever of workers power; corporatist and hybrid-authoritarian regimes ban or choke strikes, socialist feminism defends them more freely.

notes.COA: Hybrid regimes keep unions legal but channel disputes into official mediation and penalise wildcat strikes (Russia, Turkey): 2.
notes.STC: Estado Novo Estatuto do Trabalho Nacional (1933) made strikes and lockouts crimes, so it agrees only with the restraint, not the permission: 1.
notes.NAS: Falange 27 points reject class struggle and strikes in favour of vertical syndicates, but its social radicalism stops short of total agreement: 1.
notes.SF: Strikes are the main collective weapon against capital and unpaid care labour (Bread and Roses, 1912; Italian wages-for-housework): -1.
notes.CO: Etzioni and Sandel stress mediation and shared obligation over confrontation: 2.
notes.LIF: Treats the right to strike as legitimate yet normally a last step after bargaining; adherents differ on how strictly: 1.
